scope: Second ten explicitly approved and removed; deleted cards retain IDs and reasons only.

removals.TCS-2996: Theorem 8 gives an O((2-epsilon)^n) algorithm for some constant epsilon>0, explicitly answering introductory Open Problem 1. The general all-k target is separate. Source: https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.ICALP.2021.113 (Open Problem 1 and Theorem 8, PDF pages 2-3).
removals.TCS-2364: The paper proves the matching Omega(n alpha_k(n)) edge lower bound for (1+epsilon)-spanners and all hop bounds k, explicitly settling its historical Question 1.1. Source: https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.SoCG.2023.47 (Abstract and Question 1.1).
removals.TCS-2655: The paper resolves Hanneke Open Problem 3: the class SUOL is invariant across the specified separable near-metric output spaces with bounded nontrivial loss. Source: https://proceedings.mlr.press/v178/blanchard22a.html (Section 2.3, Open Problem 3, PDF page 6; following construction).
removals.TCS-3003: The main theorem constructs a GSF-local graph property without the required testing behavior, resolving the quoted universal non-propagation question negatively. Source: https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2021.34 (Theorem 1, introductory Question 7).
removals.TCS-5503: The Delayed Lossy-Link model always has a perpetual broadcaster but makes stabilizing consensus impossible, explicitly answering the quoted sufficiency question negatively. Source: https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.OPODIS.2024.18 (Abstract and introduction, PDF pages 1-3).
removals.TCS-4717: The source supplies constant-round commitments under post-quantum one-way functions, answering Question 1 for its standard non-malleability-with-respect-to-commitments notion. Stronger variants are separate. Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.05861 (FOCS 2023 Question 1, PDF page 2; abstract and construction).
removals.TCS-6076: Theorem 3 supplies the requested non-degenerate graph class using friendship graphs and tolerates multiple semi-honest corruptions. The existential feasibility target is answered, without asserting feasibility for every graph family. Source: https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.ITC.2024.1 (Theorem 3, PDF page 6).
removals.TCS-5028: The source proves a matching Omega((L/mu) log(1/epsilon)) gradient-oracle lower bound within its first-order model, establishing gradient-descent optimality up to numerical constants for general smooth PL functions. Source: https://proceedings.mlr.press/v195/yue23a.html (Abstract; motivating question and algorithm model, PDF page 4).
removals.TCS-1487: The cited paper answers the quoted standard-conversion canonicity question affirmatively and reports a mechanized proof for Exceptional Type Theory. This is not a claim that this review reran the formalization. Source: https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.FSCD.2026.26 (Section 4, PDF page 13; abstract).
removals.TCS-6333: The CONCUR 2022 source settles the case without tests and leaves the test extension open. The authors' LMCS 2024 journal extension proves completeness also with tests, resolving the remaining scope ambiguity. Source: https://lmcs.episciences.org/14369 (CONCUR 2022 PDF page 4; LMCS 2024 abstract, relational completeness theorem).
